claim_tested: Does the Zn have a cofactor-like coordination sphere?
key_finding: Zn has exactly one protein ligand, Cys54 SG at 2.22 +/- 0.05 A, plus 2-3 waters; occupancy 0.67 in all 4 chains; bond valence sum 1.16 vs 2.0 expected. Internal controls in the same model: Ca BVS 2.05, Na BVS 0.90.
confidence_and_limitations: High. Bond valence is calibrated by the two control ions in the same structure. Single crystal form.

claim_tested: Is the Zn buried in a structural loop or exposed in the cleft?
key_finding: Zn SASA 13.4 A^2 with waters removed, versus 1.2 A^2 for the Ca ion; Zn lies 3.3-3.5 A from the sulfonate oxygens of the MES buffer bound in the substrate groove.
confidence_and_limitations: High. SASA computed by Shrake-Rupley, 512 points, 1.4 A probe.

claim_tested: Does the Zn bridge the Cys54-His117 dyad as a catalytic metal would?
key_finding: Zn-Cys54 SG 2.22 A, Zn-His117 ND1 4.23 A, Zn-Glu134 OE1 8.92 A; Zn-SG-His117 ND1 angle 87 deg. The Zn caps the nucleophile from the solvent side rather than bridging the dyad.

claim_tested: Is the Zn a modelling error?
key_finding: Zn RSCC 0.986, RSR 0.034, completeness 1.0, zero clashes; better fitted than the MES (RSCC 0.870) and glycerol (0.798) in the same groove.
confidence_and_limitations: High. Density fit shows the ion is really there; it says nothing about biological relevance.

evidence_type: direct assay (X-ray fluorescence) and review of own structure
key_finding: The presence of calcium and zinc ions in the structure was confirmed by X-ray fluorescence emission spectroscopy. The same paper states "A zinc ion was found more loosely bound."
confidence_and_limitations: High for element identity. The authors themselves do not claim a catalytic zinc.

claim_tested: Is the site specific for zinc?
key_finding: In the methylmercury derivative, methylmercury occupies the same position on Cys54 SG at 2.47 A in all four chains (occupancy 0.67-0.80) while the Ca site is unchanged. No Zn is modelled.
confidence_and_limitations: High. Shows the site is a promiscuous soft-metal trap on a reactive thiolate.

citation: 16 CHAP structures in the PDB (recomputed here)
claim_tested: Is zinc a feature of CHAP domains?
key_finding: Zinc occurs in 1 of 16 CHAP coordinate sets (4CSH) and is the only Cys-bound metal anywhere in the set. Calcium occurs in 5, and the LysGH15 CHAP (4OLK) uses the identical ligands Asp45, Asp47, Tyr49-O, His51-O, Asp56.
context: PF05257 entries incl. PlyC 4F88, PcsB 9R7G, lysin L1/L2 11CF/11CG, Ly7917 5D74/5D76, LysIME-EF1 6IST, PlyGRCS 8H1I
confidence_and_limitations: High for the deposited set. Crystallisation conditions differ between entries, so absence of Ca in some entries is not proof of absence in solution.

claim_tested: Are zinc ligands conserved relative to the catalytic dyad?
key_finding: No separate zinc-ligand set exists: the only protein ligand is the catalytic Cys. Identity among aligned homologs: Cys54 98.0%, His117 99.4%, Glu134 64.1%; Ca ligands Asp47 92.5%, Asp56 93.2%, Asp45 49.2% identical and 97.7% D/N/E.
context: 132 phage and 42 reviewed bacterial CHAP sequences, Smith-Waterman BLOSUM62, gap -11/-1, score cutoff 60
confidence_and_limitations: Medium-high. Pairwise alignment rather than a curated profile alignment; Tyr49 and His51 donate main-chain O so side-chain identity is not informative.

claim_tested: Does zinc activate or inhibit a CHAP-domain enzyme?
key_finding: Chelation by addition of EDTA or the addition of zinc inhibited the activity of all PlyTW constructs. and "Addition of Ca(2+) enhanced the turbidity reduction activity of both the full length protein and truncation constructs harboring the CHAP domain."
context: Twort phage endolysin PlyTW, CHAP 46.6% identical to CHAP_K over 131 aligned residues, live S. aureus
confidence_and_limitations: High for direction of effect. Homolog rather than LysK itself; zinc concentration not stated in the abstract.

claim_tested: Is calcium the activity-supporting cation for CHAP domains?
key_finding: The phiSH2 endolysin CHAP domain activity "was further enhanced by the presence of bivalent calcium ions."
context: Staphylococcus haemolyticus prophage phiSH2 endolysin, staphylococcal strains
confidence_and_limitations: Medium-high. Homolog; enhancement not quantified in the abstract.

stance: supports calcium site, silent on zinc
claim_tested: Are the metal-site residues required for activity?
key_finding: Site-directed mutagenesis was used to demonstrate that residues involved in calcium binding and of the proposed active site were important for enzyme activity. No mutant tests any zinc-specific ligand, because none exists apart from Cys54.
confidence_and_limitations: Medium. Zymograms are qualitative; Cys54 mutation cannot separate catalysis from zinc binding.

key_finding: Site-directed mutagenesis indicated that this calcium ion is involved in the catalytic mechanism of the enzyme.
confidence_and_limitations: Low-medium. Review-level phrasing. The Ca sits 9.75 A from Cys54 SG, so a direct catalytic role is not geometrically possible; a structural requirement is the parsimonious reading.

claim_tested: Which domain of LysK carries the lytic activity?
key_finding: CHAP-only truncations lyse S. aureus in zymogram, plate lysis and turbidity assays; cleavage is between D-alanine of the stem peptide and glycine of the cross-bridge.
context: LysK truncations, live S. aureus and purified peptidoglycan, ESI-MS

stance: refutes both catalytic and structural zinc
claim_tested: Does the CHAP_K zinc resemble zinc sites of known role?
key_finding: Protein ligands and bond valence: CHAP_K Zn 1 ligand / BVS 1.12; carbonic anhydrase II 3 / 2.13; thermolysin 4 / 2.17; ADH catalytic 3 / 2.20; ADH Cys4 structural 4 / 2.05; Zif268 4 / 2.23; T7 lysozyme Amidase_2 catalytic zinc 3 / 1.30. Every reference site has 3-4 protein ligands at occupancy 1.00; the CHAP_K zinc has 1 at occupancy 0.67.
context: reference zinc enzymes and zinc fingers, 1.0-2.0 A
confidence_and_limitations: High for ligand count, which separates the classes without overlap. BVS is the weaker discriminator since the T7 lysozyme zinc also scores low from long bonds at 2.0 A.

claim_tested: Where does the zinc annotation on LysK come from?
key_finding: Zn(2+) binding sites are annotated at His214, His324, Cys332 with ECO:0000250 (by similarity), inside the amidase-2 domain 205-334, not in the CHAP domain 29-160. Ca(2+) sites 45/47/49/51/56 carry ECO:0000269. GO has GO:0046872 IEA from keyword only; no GO:0008270 and no GO:0005509.
confidence_and_limitations: High for the record contents. The amidase-2 zinc is itself a prediction with no LysK structure.
